recheck.issue: quiz 4-6-q4 why: 'only the order matters is true when everyone is sorted by probability alone' ignores group-specific miscalibration
recheck.reason: slices.by_size: small 17.6% predicted vs 18.3% actual, large 5.5% vs 8.4%. A probability that runs low in one group also pushes that group down a probability-sorted list; order is unaffected only by a shift common to everyone.
recheck.change: Second sentence of why rewritten: 'Only the order matters' holds when every score is off in the same way; when percentages run low in one group, that group sits too low on any list, sorted by probability or by dollars. The key (option 3) is unchanged.
